topic: understanding the concept of a coordinate plane reflection

easy.text: If point (3, 5) is reflected over the x-axis, what is the new point?

options.feedback: Correct -- reflecting over the x-axis flips the sign of the y-coordinate, keeping x the same.
This flips the x-coordinate instead of the y-coordinate, which would be a reflection over the y-axis instead.
This flips both coordinates, which would represent a reflection through the origin, not just over the x-axis.
This swaps the coordinates entirely, which isn't how a simple reflection over the x-axis works.

medium.text: If point (-4, 6) is reflected over the y-axis, what is the new point?

options.feedback: Correct -- reflecting over the y-axis flips the sign of the x-coordinate, keeping y the same.
This flips the y-coordinate instead of the x-coordinate, which would be a reflection over the x-axis instead.
This flips both coordinates, which would represent a reflection through the origin, not just over the y-axis.
This swaps the coordinates entirely, which isn't how a simple reflection over the y-axis works.

hard.text: A point (2, -7) is reflected over the x-axis, and then that new point is reflected over the y-axis. What is the final resulting point?

options.feedback: Correct -- first reflecting over the x-axis gives (2, 7), then reflecting that over the y-axis gives (-2, 7).
This only performs the first reflection (over the x-axis), forgetting the second reflection over the y-axis.
This only performs the second reflection correctly on the ORIGINAL point, without first applying the x-axis reflection.
This swaps the coordinates entirely, which isn't the result of these two sequential reflections.

easy.hard: This transformation flips the sign of just one coordinate, corresponding to the axis of reflection.
easy.medium: Flip the sign of the y-coordinate, but keep the x-coordinate the same.

medium.hard: This transformation flips the sign of just one coordinate, corresponding to the axis of reflection.
medium.medium: Flip the sign of the x-coordinate, but keep the y-coordinate the same.

hard.hard: Apply each reflection transformation one at a time, in the given order, updating the point after each individual step.
hard.medium: First flip the y-coordinate's sign, then take that new point and flip its x-coordinate's sign.
hard.easy: First change -7 to 7, then change that 2 to -2.
